note: Proposed before any suggestion result was seen, for the release owner to approve or change. Do not loosen a threshold after seeing a failure. 'required' gates block release; a gate that is not_measured blocks too. The assessor gates read the labels TESDA assessors give through evaluation.labeling (source file:suggestion_assessor_v1).

gates.why: The lower end of the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of Recall@3(suggest) minus Recall@3(baseline) is above zero for keyword-only, semantic-only, most-popular and random. If suggest() cannot beat a static list, it is not personalising.
At least 80% of the suggestions learners would see are rated relevant (2) or strongly relevant (3) by assessors.
At most 1 in 20 shown suggestions is rated irrelevant: a bad nudge costs more than no nudge.
For profiles with an appropriate qualification, one appears in the three shown (abstaining counts as a miss).
Passport-present and hints-only learners get recall within 0.10 of everyone's.
No skills, no suggestion, without exception.
A lone soft skill such as 'communication' says nothing about a trade.
Skills outside TVET get nothing rather than the nearest trade.
Matches matching's own rejection floor (model_acceptance.json: rejection 0.9).
Engineering check on team-written labels before assessor labels exist; not a release claim.
Engineering check on team-written labels before assessor labels exist.
On real Skill Passport profiles, the five most-shown qualifications take at most 40% of what is shown.
No single qualification takes more than 15% of what real learners are shown.
Every region with enough learners to report is within 0.10 of the overall share left without a suggestion.

agreement.why: Assessor labels count only once independent raters agree (Krippendorff's tentative floor; 0.8 for firm conclusions). Read from evaluation.labeling's agreement report.

sample.why: With 150 profiles a Recall@3 difference of about 0.10 is detectable; every profile needs two raters for agreement.
